CANONICAL_NAME.value: libcorrect -- convolutional (Viterbi) and Reed-Solomon forward error correction in C (Brian Armstrong, Quiet Modem Project)

VERSION.value: github.com/quiet/libcorrect master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: A portable SUCCESSOR/RIVAL to Phil Karn's libfec (in the vault as libfec-karn, BLOCKED by its 32-bit x86 assembly): the same two code families -- convolutional codes decoded by Viterbi, and Reed-Solomon over GF(2^8) -- reimplemented in plain C with SSE optional, plus a libfec-compatible shim. Its tests are the ADVERSARIAL PAIR: a noise/erasure injector corrupts codewords, the decoders must recover them. Deepens the ECC lineage: Rockliff RS (1991) -> Karn libfec (1990s-2000s) -> libcorrect (2016-).

value.built_to: carry data across a channel that flips or erases symbols, and recover the message exactly
value.pressure: noise, erasures, burst errors; portability pressure that killed the assembly-bound predecessor
value.success_means: every codeword corrupted within the design bound decodes to the original message; beyond the bound, failure is detected or reported

value.pressure: channel noise, symbol erasure, CPU/platform diversity
value.failure_condition: miscorrection: the decoder returns the wrong message with confidence
